payload.explanation: Monitor mon_ed2cace5e4f1 (effort_event, finger_joint, le 10, from u_brown's contract clause invariants.grasp_effort_instantaneous / raw_spec.limits.max_clamp_effort=10) fired during grasp_skill(object_id=u_brown) at wall_ns 1792104784302677000, triggering_value 28.1867. get_evidence on joint_states/finger_joint across the surrounding window shows effort flat near 0 during approach/pre-close, then a sharp monotonic ramp starting at wall_ns ~1792104784181574000 (5.23) through 10.95, 20.41, 28.19 (the fire) and continuing up to a sustained plateau around 62.6 that holds steady for the following ~2 seconds while finger_joint position holds fixed at 0.6329. This is not a brief contact transient: the gripper closed past the point of first contact and continued driving into the part, settling at a clamp force roughly 6x the part's tolerated max_clamp_effort of 10. The mechanism is an over-torqued grasp close -- the gripper commanded a close force/width that did not respect u_brown's tolerated clamp effort, producing sustained over-clamping on a part whose contract caps it at 10. This directly violates invariants.grasp_effort_instantaneous and is not a valid variation, since no clause permits exceeding the registry's max_clamp_effort for this part.

payload.explanation: Monitor mon_90f1a3ed3154 (relative_frame, parent=tcp, child=line_green, max_delta_m=0.02, from the instruction's in-hand-slippage invariant, threshold sourced from raw_spec.tolerances.grasp_slip_tolerance_m=0.02) fired at wall_ns 1792105116800161000 during move_grasp_center_to_pose descent in place_line_green, triggering_value 0.02038 vs the 0.0761m reference captured at the grasp phase. get_evidence on object_poses(line_green) and frames(tcp) over the surrounding window shows the mechanism directly: tcp descended smoothly and continuously (z from ~0.183 to ~0.128 over the window) while line_green's own z stayed essentially flat (~0.0742, barely moving) and its x/y also stayed nearly fixed. Pairing the closest-in-time samples at the fire instant gives a straight-line tcp-to-object distance of ~0.0558m versus the ~0.0761m grasp-time reference, a genuine ~2.03cm reduction in separation. Over the same window finger_joint position held essentially constant (0.5403-0.5404 rad, no reopening or reclosing), ruling out an intentional width change as the explanation per the relative_frame monitor's own documented caveat. The physical picture is that line_green shifted roughly 2cm relative to the closed gripper while the arm continued its placement descent -- the part rode/slipped within the jaws rather than tracking the gripper rigidly, consistent with the part settling against the fixture surface (or shifting under approach-induced contact) before the jaws released it. This is a real in-hand slippage violation of the instruction's invariant that a held part must not move relative to the gripper before release; it is not a mis-arming, since the reference was captured correctly at the 'grasped' phase and the drift tracks a physically coherent event (object stalling while tcp kept moving), not sensor noise (no discontinuity, monotonic trend, finger width unchanged).

At end_step for place_line_green the executor itself claimed_outcome=\"failure\", reporting final_position error 0.0219m against position_tolerance_m 0.015 and orientation error 24.6deg against orientation_tolerance_deg 10 (both from line_green's raw_spec.tolerances). query_snapshot confirms this independently: line_green at (0.40343,-0.19903,0.07426) vs line_green_placement at (0.40392,-0.20003,0.05238), a ~0.0219m position gap concentrated almost entirely in z (part sitting ~2.2cm too high), consistent with the in-hand-slippage finding already recorded for this same step: the part separated from the gripper's planned trajectory mid-descent (tcp kept descending while line_green's height stalled at ~0.074, short of the placement z of 0.0524) and never reached its seat. This is the direct consequence of that slip, not an independent failure mode: the part came to rest resting on/near the fixture surface above its intended seated depth and rotated off-axis (24.6deg) rather than settling flush. This is an end_step evidence check that fails the effects clause even though the slip fire already covered the proximate cause; it is recorded as its own finding because the seating requirement is a distinct effect clause from the slip invariant and both are due at this milestone.

payload.explanation: Monitor mon_fab963513f4a (relative_frame, tcp vs line_green, max_delta_m=0.02, in-hand-slippage invariant, threshold raw_spec.tolerances.grasp_slip_tolerance_m=0.02) fired at wall_ns 1792105310300044500 during the unplanned recovery step reseat_line_green_place (not on the expected process map; it is a reattempt of place_line_green after the earlier missed seat), triggering_value 0.020245. get_evidence on object_poses(line_green), frames(tcp) and joint_states(finger_joint) across the window shows a much more severe event than the first slip: line_green's orientation quaternion y-component swings from near 0 to about -0.45 (a rotation of roughly 50+ degrees) while tcp's own orientation stays essentially fixed throughout, meaning the part physically rotated inside the closed jaws. This coincides with a large finger_joint effort excursion, climbing from a resting ~8.3 up to a peak of ~144 (still under line_green's 170 clamp limit, so no separate clamp-effort violation) before settling back near 40-50, and with finger_joint position drifting from 0.5404 down to about 0.5385 and partially back -- a real, if small, width change consistent with the part shifting and the jaws re-seating around it. The physical picture is the part slipping/rotating significantly in the gripper during this second place attempt, most likely because it was regrasped from its fallen, off-axis resting pose from the first attempt (confirmed orientation error 24.6deg) and the new grasp did not fully stabilize it before the carry-and-lower motion began. This is a genuine in-hand-slippage violation, not a mis-arming: the reference was captured correctly at this step's own 'grasped' phase and the drift tracks a coherent physical event (sustained rotation plus effort spike) rather than isolated noise.

At end_step for the unplanned recovery step reseat_line_green_place, the executor itself claimed_outcome="failure" with final_position error 0.03m (threshold 0.015m) and orientation error 43.8deg (threshold 10deg), noting the motion reported SUCCESS to the exact target but line_green tipped/shifted after release, worse than the first attempt. query_snapshot confirms independently: line_green at (0.40543,-0.19908,0.08245) vs line_green_placement at (0.40517,-0.20015,0.05238), a ~0.0301m gap concentrated in z (part sitting ~3cm above seat), with a large rotation matching the severe in-hand-slip/rotation already recorded during this same step's carry phase (orientation quaternion y-component drifted to ~-0.45). This is the direct consequence of that slip: the part rotated substantially in the gripper before release and so landed off-axis and high of its seat on this second attempt as well. u_brown and u_orange remain at their prior recorded poses (position deltas <0.002m, well within their 0.02m disturbance tolerance) and base1 likewise essentially unmoved (~0.0013m), so neither was disturbed by this recovery attempt.

payload.explanation:
This is the run's final end-state verdict, covering all steps from run start to run_ended (status "completed"). Measured independently via query_snapshot at run end: u_brown vs u_brown_placement error 0.00206m (tol 0.01m); u_orange vs u_orange_placement error 0.0022m (tol 0.02m); line_green vs line_green_placement error 0.0066m (tol 0.015m); inverted_u_yellow vs inverted_u_yellow_placement error 0.00152m (tol 0.012m) -- all four parts seated within tolerance with negligible orientation error. base1 and all four bystanders (u_green, inverted_u_brown, hex_blue, hex_red) measured against their run-start reference poses show sub-millimeter deltas, far inside the 0.02m disturbance tolerance, and no stationarity monitor fired for any of them across the entire run.

Findings during the run: (1) pick_u_brown -- the clamp-effort invariant (<=10) was violated, with finger_joint effort climbing to a sustained plateau of ~62.6 during the grasp close, roughly 6x the limit; the executor's own claim under-reported this as 28.19. This is a genuine invariant breach but it left no lasting positional defect -- u_brown's final pose is within tolerance and the elevated effort is not present at run end (gripper now open, effort ~0), so nothing from it stands uncorrected at the end-state level; it is recorded as a timeline finding only. (2) place_line_green -- line_green slipped/rotated in the gripper (relative_frame delta 0.02038 vs 0.02 tolerance) and missed its seat (0.0219m / 24.6deg off, both exceeding tolerance); the executor then reopened the task under an unplanned step sequence (reseat_line_green_pick / reseat_line_green_place_approach / reseat_line_green_place -- none on the expected process map, named here as unplanned), during which the part slipped again, more severely (delta 0.02024, rotation ~50deg) and again missed its seat (0.0301m / 43.8deg off). (3) A second unplanned recovery sequence, reseat2_line_green_pick / reseat2_line_green_place_approach / reseat2_line_green_place, succeeded cleanly: no slip fire, and the part landed within tolerance (0.0066m / 0.4deg). Throughout all of this, u_brown, u_orange and base1 were never disturbed (every check held within their disturbance tolerance), confirming the recovery attempts did not collaterally damage already-seated work.

End-state conclusion: every part's final pose meets its placement frame within tolerance, base1 and all bystanders are undisturbed, and the line_green seating defect found mid-run was fully corrected by the second recovery attempt -- a genuine recovery, not a lucky pass, since the mechanism (slip during descent) was identified from evidence both times it occurred. The u_brown clamp-effort violation remains on the record as a real process defect but does not correspond to any unresolved end-state condition, so per the decision rule (non_conformant requires a wrong final pose or a violation still standing) the run's end-state is conformant.
